provenance.reference: NASA JPL (2020) NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second NC V001, doi:10.5067/MEaSUREs/NASADEM/NASADEM_NC.001, via AppEEARS

provenance.item: Slope and aspect from a 3x3 window
provenance.reference: Horn, B.K.P. (1981) Hill shading and the reflectance map, Proc. IEEE 69(1):14-47; weights recalled, not re-read, and checked by tests on exact planes

provenance.item: RUSLE slope steepness factor S and slope length factor L
provenance.reference: Renard et al. (1997) USDA Agriculture Handbook 703, after McCool et al. (1987, 1989); formulas recalled, not re-read, and checked against the unit plot (LS = 1 at 22.13 m and 9%)
FAO Guidelines for Soil Description (2006) slope classes, recalled; to be checked against the FAO text

provenance.reference: Rotavise reading aid; not a published erosion class

provenance.item: Maximum slope length 300 m and vertical noise 3 m
provenance.reference: Recalled RUSLE practice and NASADEM accuracy; low confidence

provenance.item: Cold-air pooling hint (5 m below surroundings, slope under 5%)
provenance.reference: Topographic position index idea (Weiss 2001); thresholds are Rotavise heuristics

limitations: A digital surface model from the year 2000 radar mission, resampled to 30 m: trees, buildings and later earthworks are not what the ground looks like today.
Heights carry a vertical error of a few metres; slopes below about 6.4% cannot be told apart from noise.
Erosion is a relative reading (RUSLE LS factor): it ignores rainfall, soil, cover and flow paths, and is not a soil-loss figure.
The cold-air hint compares the field with points 300 m and 600 m away; it is not a frost forecast and needs local confirmation.

products: ECO_L2T_LSTE.002 land surface temperature (70 m) via AppEEARS
ECO_L4T_ESI.002 evaporative stress index PT-JPL (70 m) via AppEEARS

provenance.item: ECOSTRESS tiled land surface temperature and evaporative stress index
provenance.reference: NASA JPL ECOSTRESS ECO_L2T_LSTE.002 and ECO_L4T_ESI.002 via AppEEARS (dois 10.5067/ECOSTRESS/ECO_L2T_LSTE.002, 10.5067/ECOSTRESS/ECO_L4T_ESI.002)
Rotavise summary: clear pixels averaged per acquisition, then per month; no threshold is applied

limitations: The space station passes at changing times and not every day, and cloud removes many scenes: a month's mean is a sample of that month, not a full record.
Land surface temperature is the temperature of the ground and leaves, not air temperature; it is not used as a frost or heat limit.
The evaporative stress index (0 to 1) compares actual with potential evapotranspiration; low values suggest plant water stress but do not name a cause.

result.product: MOD13Q1.061 vegetation indices (250 m, 16 day) via AppEEARS

provenance.reference: Didan, K. (2021) MOD13Q1 MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m SIN Grid V061, NASA LP DAAC, doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13Q1.061, via AppEEARS
NASA Earthdata data alert 'Transition from MODIS to VIIRS', issued 2 May 2025 (earthdata.nasa.gov/data/alerts-outages/transition-from-modis-viirs), read on 2026-11-08
Rotavise keeps pixels whose reliability layer is 0 (good data) and drops marginal, snow, ice and cloudy ones; nothing is filled in

limitations: Each value covers a 250 m pixel, about 6 hectares: a small field shares its pixel with its surroundings, so the neighbour comparison matters.
Sixteen-day composites pick the best clear day in each period, so a short change of a week can be missed.

NASA's data alert of 2 May 2025 says Terra and Aqua begin shutting down in late 2026 or early 2027 and MODIS data will no longer be collected, and that both platforms are drifting from their designed orbits, which can affect crossing times and data; later dates may stop arriving.
